researchNote: Official primary sources only (direct fetch of vendor docs and vendor doc repos; directory search API unavailable at research time). Anything not stated in official docs is marked UNSPECIFIED. No community sources used; no live-provider calls.

codex-cli.alwaysOnNotes: Global ~/.codex/AGENTS.md or AGENTS.override.md; per-directory AGENTS.override.md > AGENTS.md > configured fallback filenames; root-down concatenation; combined cap 32KiB.
codex-cli.precedence: deeper file loads later and overrides; one file per directory, override kills base
codex-cli.reviewChannel: ## Code Review Rules section in nearest AGENTS.md; root + file-specific both apply per changed file
codex-cli.foreignFiles: only via configured fallback filenames or one-time /import

claude-code.alwaysOnNotes: Managed policy -> ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md -> ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md -> CLAUDE.local.md; ancestor chain plus on-demand subdir loads; @path imports. AGENTS.md is NOT read natively.
claude-code.precedence: concatenation root-down (ordering only, no override); enterprise > personal > project for skills
claude-code.foreignFiles: never native; needs @AGENTS.md import/symlink or one-time /init|/import

gemini-cli.alwaysOnNotes: Global ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md -> workspace + parents -> JIT discovery on tool access; concatenation; @file imports; filename configurable via context.fileName (any name, including AGENTS.md).
gemini-cli.precedence: UNSPECIFIED between concatenated GEMINI.md levels (load order stated, no override rule)
packaging: gemini extensions (prompts + MCP + commands + hooks + skills)

copilot-chat.alwaysOnNotes: Repo: .github/copilot-instructions.md + .github/instructions/**/*.instructions.md + agent files (VS Code chat reads AGENTS.md; github.com chat reads agents-only set). Personal/org instructions on github.com only.
copilot-chat.precedence: personal > path-specific > repo-wide > agent files > org (all supplied, nondeterministic merge)
copilot-chat.foreignFiles: VS Code chat reads AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md natively

copilot-coding-agent.alwaysOnNotes: Repo-wide + path-specific + agent-ALL set (AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md + GEMINI.md) + org; nested AGENTS.md anywhere with nearest-wins; single root CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md as the alternative.
copilot-coding-agent.precedence: personal > path-specific > repo-wide > agent files > org (all supplied)

copilot-review.alwaysOnNotes: Repo-wide + path-specific + agent-ONLY set (AGENTS.md; CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md are NOT eligible); repo settings toggle; instructions and skills sourced from the HEAD branch (testable in-PR).
copilot-review.precedence: personal > path-specific > repo-wide > agent files > org (all supplied)
copilot-review.reviewChannel: AGENTS.md-only channel with repo toggle + HEAD-branch sourcing

vscode-agent-mode.alwaysOnNotes: Combines copilot-instructions.md + AGENTS.md (nested, experimental, setting-gated) + CLAUDE.md + *.instructions.md (applyTo) + .claude/rules (paths) + org; NO merge order guaranteed; user > repo > org on conflict; per-type settings toggles.
vscode-agent-mode.scopedSyntax: .github/instructions/**/*.instructions.md with applyTo glob; .claude/rules with paths array
vscode-agent-mode.precedence: combined with NO guaranteed order; conflicting rules are unsafe here

notes: One managed file does not cover all CLIs natively (D1); ACKit emits the per-provider set.
Codex/Gemini skill content equals the SKILL.md open standard (N2); roots differ (D3) and are caller-chosen via --out, so no separate codex/gemini export targets exist.
Scoped rules are authored once and projected to applyTo (copilot/vscode) and paths (claude) dialects where the surface requires it (D5).

differences.statement: The canonical always-on filename is provider-specific (AGENTS.md vs CLAUDE.md vs GEMINI.md vs .github/copilot-instructions.md); one file does not cover all CLIs natively.

Foreign-file reading differs: Claude never reads AGENTS.md natively; Codex only via fallback filenames or import; Gemini reads any filename via context.fileName; VS Code and the Copilot cloud agent are multi-native.
Skills discovery roots differ (.agents/skills vs .claude/skills vs .gemini/skills vs .github/skills); one payload directory does not serve every provider.
Skills name-conflict resolution differs (Codex shows both; Gemini higher tier wins; Claude enterprise > personal > project with dir-qualified nested names).
Scoped-instruction syntax differs (paths: array vs applyTo: glob vs nested files vs JIT discovery); one scoped rule needs per-surface rendering.

Precedence semantics differ (Codex deeper-overrides; Claude concat-ordering; Copilot personal > path > wide > agent > org; VS Code no guaranteed order), so conflicting rules are unsafe on VS Code but ordered elsewhere.
The code-review instruction channel differs (Codex ## Code Review Rules section in AGENTS.md vs Copilot review AGENTS.md-only channel with repo toggle and HEAD-branch sourcing).
Size caps differ and bound emission (Codex 32KiB combined AGENTS.md; Claude 4MiB skip with <200-line guidance; Copilot review ~1000-line guidance).
Distribution packaging differs (Gemini extensions vs Codex plugins vs VS Code chatSkills contribution vs Claude plugins); one manifest does not install everywhere.
VS Code file support is settings-gated (useAgentsMdFile/useClaudeMdFile/nested/locations toggles plus review/commit/PR instruction settings); repo files alone are insufficient there.

nonDifferences.statement: All surfaces load instructions as context; none enforces them (Copilot nondeterministic; Claude context-not-config; Codex review guides but never replaces tests/approvals). Same caveat everywhere.
Skill authoring converged on the Agent Skills open standard (SKILL.md with required name+description) across Claude, Codex, Gemini, and VS Code/Copilot: author once, project to multiple roots.
Frontmatter invocation controls (user-invocable / disable-model-invocation, fork context) are shared Claude/VS Code/Copilot vocabulary, not differentiators.
All surfaces share the two-tier shape (user/global + repo/project always-on, concatenated); differences are only filenames, ordering semantics (D6), and caps (D8).
Progressive disclosure for skills (metadata first, body on activation) is universal.
